16	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.service;
17	
18	/**
19	 * Thrown when an attempt is made to create an {@code Owner} in a city that already contains the
20	 * maximum number of owners ({@value #MAX_OWNERS_PER_CITY}). Enforcing it in the service layer keeps
21	 * the capacity invariant in one place regardless of which caller initiates the create; the REST
22	 * layer maps this to a {@code 409 Conflict}.
23	 */
24	public class CityOwnerLimitExceededException extends RuntimeException {
25	
26	    public static final int MAX_OWNERS_PER_CITY = 50;
27	
28	    public CityOwnerLimitExceededException(String city) {
29	        super("The city '" + city + "' already contains the maximum of " + MAX_OWNERS_PER_CITY + " owners");
30	    }
31	
32	}

content.text:
VERDICT: LGTM

The change slots cleanly into the existing patterns:

- `DailyOwnerLimitExceededException` is a faithful sibling of `CityOwnerLimitExceededException` — same package, same `MAX_*` constant convention, same message-building style, same service-layer-invariant rationale in the javadoc.
- `countOwnersRegisteredOn(LocalDate)` mirrors the existing private `countOwnersInCity` / `countNamesakes` helpers exactly (same `ownerRepository.findAll().stream().filter(...).count()` idiom, same "already exist (before this create)" javadoc phrasing). It lives in the right unit next to the other count helpers.
- The guard in `saveOwner` is placed consistently alongside the other `owner.isNew() && count... >= MAX` checks, in a sensible order.
- The `ExceptionControllerAdvice` handler is a direct copy of the surrounding handler shape (logging, `detailBuild`, `ResponseEntity.status(...)`), differing only in the 429 status the spec requires.

Nothing is duplicated beyond the deliberate parallel structure, and no class is becoming a catch-all. A maintainer of this codebase would find it natural.
